title: Left fractions and localized retractions in a Brown cofibration category
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, mapping spaces and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a universe containing the categories involved. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with an initial object $0$ and classes $C,W$ containing isomorphisms and closed under composition. Assume $W$ is retract closed and has two-out-of-three, every $0\to X$ lies in $C$, every arrow factors as a member of $C$ followed by a member of $W$, pushouts of members of $C$ along arbitrary arrows exist and belong to $C$, and pushouts of members of $C\cap W$ belong to $C\cap W$. Let $q:N\mathcal A\to L$ be a localization: for every quasicategory $\mathcal D$, restriction identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal D)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal A,\mathcal D)$ inverting $W$.
Write $hL$ for the category with the objects of $L$ and morphisms $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_L(x,y)$. Every object of $L$ is equivalent to some $qX$. For any $X,Y\in\mathcal A$, every arrow $\alpha:qX\to qY$ has, in $hL$, a representative
$$[\alpha]=[q(s)]^{-1}[q(f)],\qquad f:X\to Z,\quad s:Y\to Z\text{ in }C\cap W.$$
For an ordinary arrow $u:X\to Y$, $[q(u)]$ has a left inverse in $hL$ if and only if there exist $Z$ and $i:Y\to Z$ in $C$ with $iu\in W$. No saturation assumption on $W$, functorial factorization, model structure or infinite coproducts is imposed.

source.place: Dual of Corollary 7.2.18 and formula (7.2.10.4), with the trivial fibrations of Proposition 7.4.13; dual of Corollary 7.5.19, printed pp. 380-381; essential surjectivity from the localization construction in section 7.1. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Put $T=C\cap W$. It contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary cobase change by the stated axioms. The pushout of $0\to B$ along $0\to A$ is $A\amalg B$; both coproduct inclusions belong to $C$, using the same construction in the other order. For an arrow $v:B\to A$, factor the copairing $[1_A,v]:A\amalg B\to A$ as $A\amalg B\xrightarrow{j}H\xrightarrow{r}A$, with $j\in C$, $r\in W$. Set $a=j\iota_A$ and $b=j\iota_B$. Then $ra=1_A$, $rb=v$, and $a,b\in C$. Two-out-of-three gives $a\in T$, and, if $v\in W$, also $b\in T$. All constructions are made for one arrow at a time.

source.place: Proposition 7.4.13, dual of the graph-factorization argument; Definition 7.2.20, dual split-denominator axioms.

proof.text: Enlarge the universe so that $\mathcal A$ is small and apply [lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model] to $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$, with weak equivalences $W^{\mathrm{op}}$ and denominators $T^{\mathrm{op}}$. Pushout stability and composition of $T$ give precisely its pullback and composition assumptions. For $v:B\to A$ in $W$, Step 1 provides, in the opposite category, the factorization data $s=r^{\mathrm{op}}:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to H^{\mathrm{op}}$, $p=a^{\mathrm{op}}:H^{\mathrm{op}}\to A^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $t=b^{\mathrm{op}}:H^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $ps=1$ and $ts=v^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $p,t\in T^{\mathrm{op}}$. Thus every hypothesis of the cited node holds. It gives an essentially surjective localization $q_0:N(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}})\to M$, its universal property on entire coherent functor categories, and a bijection from components of its span-category nerve to each hom-set in $hM$, sending a span to its stated fraction.

source.place: Definition 7.2.20 and Remark 7.2.21; Theorem 7.2.8, formula (7.2.10.4), and Corollary 7.2.18, applied to the opposite category.

proof.text:
Use the simplicial conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Opposite reverses the order of vertices in every simplex: an inner horn with missing face $i$ becomes the inner horn with missing face $n-i$, so $M^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory. Reversing both factors in the product defining coherent functors gives the simplicial isomorphism $\operatorname{Fun}(M^{\mathrm{op}},D)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(M,D^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$, compatible with restriction; equivalence edges remain equivalence edges because the inverse triangles reverse. Consequently the universal property in Step 2, applied to $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, makes $r=q_0^{\mathrm{op}}:N\mathcal A\to M^{\mathrm{op}}$ a localization on entire functor categories. It is essentially surjective by reversing the equivalences supplied by $q_0$.
At the level of homotopy categories, reversal gives $h(M^{\mathrm{op}})\cong(hM)^{\mathrm{op}}$. To check this with the specified pinched mapping-space convention, a right homotopy triangle between edges $f,g:x\to y$ has vertices $(x,x,y)$, edges $01=1_x$, $12=f$, $02=g$. Complete the inner $3$-horn on vertices $(x,x,y,y)$ with this face $012$, the degenerate face $123$ on $f$, and the degenerate face $013$ on $f$. The remaining face $023$ is a left homotopy triangle with edges $02=g$, $23=1_y$, $03=f$. For the reverse conversion, start with a left triangle on vertices $(x,y,y)$ and edges $01=f$, $12=1_y$, $02=g$. On vertices $(x,x,y,y)$ prescribe this as face $023$, prescribe face $123$ to be the degenerate triangle on $f$ with $12=13=f$, $23=1_y$, and prescribe face $012$ to be the degenerate triangle on $f$ with $01=1_x$, $12=02=f$. These three compatible faces form $\Lambda^3_2$; its filler gives face $013$ with $01=1_x$, $13=f$, $03=g$, the required right homotopy triangle. For any simplicial set, the classes of vertices generated by its edges are its realization components: each simplex belongs to one class and joins each of its points to a vertex, and the realization is the topological disjoint union of the subcomplexes for these classes. Thus reversing simplices preserves and reflects the equivalence relation on arrows generated by mapping-space edges. It preserves identities and reverses composition, as seen by reversing a composition triangle. This proves the asserted identification on $\pi_0$.

source.place: Section 7.1 localization universal property, duality by simplicial order reversal; elementary verification of the opposite convention used in formula (7.2.10.4).

proof.text:
Compare $r:N\mathcal A\to M^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the given localization $q:N\mathcal A\to L$. Their universal properties supply functors $F:M^{\mathrm{op}}\to L$, $G:L\to M^{\mathrm{op}}$ and coherent natural equivalences $\theta:Fr\simeq q$, $\eta:Gq\simeq r$. The restrictions of $FG$ and $1_L$ along $q$ are equivalent, since $FGq\simeq Fr\simeq q$; the equivalence of restriction functor categories therefore lifts this equivalence to $FG\simeq1_L$: apply a quasi-inverse of restriction to the equivalence and conjugate by its unit comparisons at $FG$ and $1_L$. For the other composite, $GF r\xrightarrow{G\theta}Gq\xrightarrow{\eta}r$ is a coherent natural equivalence; apply a quasi-inverse of restriction along $r$ and its unit comparisons at $GF$ and $1_{M^{\mathrm{op}}}$ to obtain $GF\simeq1_{M^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Hence $F$ is a functor equivalence. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it induces equivalences of mapping spaces, and every component $\theta_X$ is an equivalence. Therefore it gives bijections
$$\rho_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}_{h(M^{\mathrm{op}})}(rX,rY)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{hL}(qX,qY),\qquad c\longmapsto[\theta_Y]\,hF(c)\,[\theta_X]^{-1}.$$
Naturality says $[\theta_Y][F(r(u))]=[q(u)][\theta_X]$ for every ordinary $u:X\to Y$, so these bijections preserve the images of ordinary arrows, composition, identities and inverses of denominators. Also every $z\in L$ is equivalent to some $qX$: choose an equivalence $Gz\simeq rX$ by Step 3, apply $F$, and use $FGz\simeq z$ and $FrX\simeq qX$.

source.place: Definition 7.1.2 and Proposition 7.1.3: uniqueness of localization, with the quasi-inverse and comparison transformations written explicitly.

proof.text:
For $X,Y\in\mathcal A$ let $R(X,Y)$ be the ordinary category with objects $(Z,f,s)$ where $f:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$ belongs to $T$. A morphism $(Z,f,s)\to(Z',f',s')$ is an arrow $h:Z'\to Z$ satisfying $hs'=s$ and $hf'=f$. This is exactly the span category in [lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model] for source $Y^{\mathrm{op}}$ and target $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ in $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$. Step 2, reversal in Step 3, and the bijection $\rho_{X,Y}$ in Step 4 give a bijection
$$\pi_0 NR(X,Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{hL}(qX,qY),\qquad[(Z,f,s)]\longmapsto[q(s)]^{-1}[q(f)].$$
Indeed the opposite span formula is $[q_0(f^{\mathrm{op}})][q_0(s^{\mathrm{op}})]^{-1}$, whose reverse is the displayed left fraction, and the naturality equation of Step 4 removes the comparison components. Every component of this nerve contains a vertex, so this proves the fraction-representation clause with $s\in C\cap W$. The bijection also shows that equality of these homotopy-category fractions is exactly membership in the same component of $NR(X,Y)$; this injectivity, rather than a strict ordinary calculus of fractions for $W$, will be used next.

source.place: Formula (7.2.10.4) and Corollary 7.2.18, with the trivial-fibration class of Definition 7.2.20, dualized.

proof.text: In $R(X,Y)$, every comparison $h:Z'\to Z$ is in $W$: its equation $hs'=s$ has $s',s\in T\subseteq W$, so two-out-of-three applies. The other equation $hf'=f$ then gives $f'\in W$ if and only if $f\in W$. This property of a numerator is therefore constant along a finite zigzag of comparisons, in either direction. With the nerve and realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], components of a category nerve are exactly the equivalence classes of vertices generated by its arrows: each simplex has all vertices in one such class, so the nerve is the disjoint union of the subsimplicial sets for these classes; realization is the corresponding topological disjoint union, and each summand is path connected by the finite arrow zigzags. Thus the numerator property is constant on each element of $\pi_0 NR(X,Y)$.

source.place: Corollary 7.5.19, dual of the proof that weak-equivalence numerators are invariant under fraction comparisons; elementary component calculation.

proof.text: Suppose $[q(u)]$ for $u:X\to Y$ has left inverse $\beta:qY\to qX$ in $hL$. By Step 5 write $\beta=[q(s)]^{-1}[q(f)]$ with $f:Y\to Z$ and $s:X\to Z$ in $T$. The equality $\beta[q(u)]=1_{qX}$ says that the cospans $(Z,fu,s)$ and $(X,1_X,1_X)$ have equal images under the bijection of Step 5 for $R(X,X)$. They are in the same nerve component. Step 6 implies $fu\in W$, since the second numerator is an identity. Factor $f$ using the given factorization axiom as $Y\xrightarrow{i}H\xrightarrow{w}Z$, with $i\in C$ and $w\in W$. Since $w(iu)=fu\in W$, two-out-of-three gives $iu\in W$. This is the required cofibration postcomposition. The component test used here is precisely the mapping-space component bijection in [lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model], applied and identified as in Steps 2–5; it does not presume saturation.

source.place: Corollary 7.5.19, dual necessity argument and the final factorization into a cofibration followed by a weak equivalence.

proof.text: Conversely, if $i:Y\to Z$ lies in $C$ and $iu\in W$, then $[q(iu)]$ is invertible because $q$ inverts $W$. The morphism $[q(iu)]^{-1}[q(i)]:qY\to qX$ is a left inverse of $[q(u)]$, since its product with $[q(u)]$ is $[q(iu)]^{-1}[q(iu)]=1_{qX}$. Together with Steps 4, 5 and 7 this proves every clause of the unchanged statement. Retract closure was available but not needed; no extra factorization choice, saturation or coproduct hypothesis has been used.

tool_uses.why: Generic quasicategory tool: functor equivalences induce mapping-space equivalences, and coherent natural equivalences are componentwise equivalences. The Brown localization unit has no separate node supplying this basic calculus; no geometric or coefficient proof step is replaced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q35-7fc4a9ba8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all eight steps in full against Cisinski CatLR (online PDF fetched and extracted; not archived, WANTED stands): (7.2.10.4) p.336, Cor 7.2.18 and Def 7.2.20 pp.339-340, Def 7.4.12 and Prop 7.4.13 pp.365-366, Cor 7.5.19 with its proof pp.380-381. The item is their all-cofibrant ordinary dual; the statement is unchanged and not weakened. Step 1 (coproduct copairing factorization) gives ra=1 and rb=v with a,b in C∩W by 2-of-3. Step 2: I checked every hypothesis of lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model on A^op (pushout stability of T gives its pullbacks; split data s=r^op, p=a^op, t=b^op with ps=1 and ts=v^op). Step 3: I verified both inner-horn conversions (Λ^3_1 and Λ^3_2 faces, with matching edges) for the right-pinched convention of def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones. Step 4: the localization comparison and the naturality of the conjugation are correct; the cone-calculus statement gives the componentwise equivalences and mapping-space equivalences used. Step 5: the span orientation and morphism direction match R_T(Y^op,X^op), and the reversed fraction is [q s]^{-1}[q f]; injectivity on π0 comes from the cited weak-equivalence statement. Steps 6-8 (numerator invariance along W-comparisons, then factoring f to get iu in W, and the converse) match Cor 7.5.19. Edge cases: W = isomorphisms (reduces to split monos), W = all arrows, and the terminal category. No cycle (the 110-node closure excludes the item). No new nodes; I found no duplicate after an rg for Brown, fractions and cofibration (brown-split-factorizations is a model-category statement; the homotopy-fractions nodes assume a functorial calculus). The parent's Steps 5-6 use exactly the stated clauses. Accepted tool_use: lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus (unit sk-prop-sf-cbc), a generic quasicategory tool used as a black box that replaces no unit step. No SGA citation. No fixes.

The localization hypothesis uses the dependency's fullSubcomplex and IsFunctorEquivalence with the actual restriction equation; hqinverts follows from it. The homotopy category is Mathlib's HomotopyCategory (the dependency defines none) and the helpers are real data. Edge cases checked: empty/terminal category, W = isos or all arrows, identity pushouts. Universes u and v are free; one sorry, no axioms; docstrings and the Q42 second reading present. nt_compile --json on the snapshot exited 0 with no errors or warnings shown (the tool does not print the sorry warning).
